name: Zot
description: A lightweight, single-binary coding agent harness written in Go. Works with 20+ AI providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and local models. Features include four built-in tools (read, write, edit, bash), extensions via subprocess + JSON-RPC, swarm mode for background subagents, and Telegram bridge.
community_quotes: Yet another coding agent harness, but the single-binary approach with no runtime/Docker requirements is refreshing
The extension system via JSON-RPC is clever - lets you add tools in any language
Swarm mode for running parallel subagents is a unique feature I haven't seen elsewhere
License shows Copyright 2026, indicating this is a very recent project

name: OpenYabby
description: Open-source voice-driven multi-agent assistant for macOS. Combines OpenAI Realtime API for voice with CLI runners (Claude Code, Codex, Aider, etc.) to execute real tasks. Features hierarchical multi-agent orchestration, persistent memory with Mem0 + Qdrant, 30+ connectors, and multi-channel support including WhatsApp-native agent threads.
community_quotes: Featured on Hacker News as a voice-controlled multi-agent orchestrator for Claude Code
The WhatsApp-native agent threads feature is wild - spawn agents and talk to them directly in dedicated chats
Demo shows building a full SaaS with 7 coordinated agents in ~4 hours
Persistent memory across sessions with Mem0 + Qdrant actually works

name: Claw Patrol
description: Open-source security firewall for AI agents released by Deno. Sits between agents and production systems to parse and gate HTTP, SQL, Kubernetes, and SSH protocols. Addresses the critical security need of limiting AI agent access to sensitive data and systems.
community_quotes: Deno releasing Claw Patrol as an open-source agent firewall is exactly what the ecosystem needed
MIT licensed and production-ready from day one
Show HN post got 97 points and 28 comments - strong community interest

name: VEXI
description: Open-source AI coding agent for the terminal with Product Hunt launch on June 15, 2026. Bring-your-own-api-key model supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, and other providers. Built specifically for developers who prefer terminal-based workflows.
community_quotes: Featured as 'Promoted' on Product Hunt leaderboard for June 15, 2026
Terminal-based approach appeals to developers who live in the CLI
BYO API keys model keeps it flexible and privacy-friendly

name: Mira
description: Self-hosted AI code reviewer providing an open-source alternative to CodeRabbit and Greptile. Reviews pull requests using any LLM via LiteLLM with low-noise filtering including confidence thresholds, deduplication, and severity sorting. Apache 2.0 licensed.
community_quotes: Open-source alternative to expensive SaaS code reviewers is exactly what teams want
Low-noise filtering with confidence thresholds means you only see comments that matter
Works with any LLM through LiteLLM - not locked into one provider
Drop-in GitHub Action makes CI/CD integration trivial
